text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc's interim chief executive on Tuesday said the company had record sales last week and its customers were staying loyal despite its accounting problems.

The company will be an "easy turnaround," said Lawrence Ramaekers, named last week to replace Centennial's founder Emanuel Pinez, who was charged with insider trading and allegedly recorded phony sales.
"Last week I think we had an exceptional record in sales," Ramaekers told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The customers, and I've talked to a bunch of them, and they're all staying with us," he said. "I haven't had anybody tell me that they want to leave."
Ramaekers said Centennial had many customers, none of whom account for a large portion of sales.
He said most of the company's sales were legitimate. "Almost all of Centennial sales are real sales. There are some that we're questioning," he said.

Ramaekers said he spent much of the past week talking with nervous customers, employees and banks, as well as checking into the legitimacy of a myriad of small companies that Centennial had invested in or bought.
"Everything I can see, these are viable companies," he said. But he acknowledged he did not know how many companies in which Centennial had an stake or owned.
Ramaekers is a principal of Jay Alix & Associates of Southfield, Michigan, a firm specializing in turnarounds.
